subject: Deployment mode & pricing — follow-up and initial cost model
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Lee <samuel.lee@finware.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment mode & pricing — follow-up from today

Hi Samuel —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Current goal: embed summaries + question-answering in FinWare’s lending portal; latency target ~200–300ms P95 for interactive flows.
- Expected volume: ~50M tokens/month initially, with peaks during batch reconciliations.
- Primary concerns: data isolation (PII), predictable unit economics, and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Deployment modes we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, per-token pricing, Redwood handles infra and updates.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale (monthly commit).
- Private VPC / on-prem: for strict data controls and on-prem needs — longer lead time and integration work.

Next steps I suggest:
1) I’ll put together a short cost model (per-token vs reserved capacity) and highlight trade-offs for your usage profile.
2) Can you share an approximate tokens/day distribution (peak vs baseline) and whether model fine-tuning or embeddings heavy workloads are planned?
3) If procurement needs SOC2 / security artifacts, I’ll attach our SOC2 overview and a short questionnaire template.

I’ve looped in Neha from AE to support procurement cadence. I’ll follow up with an initial cost spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0126

Attachment: soc2-overview.pdf (summary, 3 pages)

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the recap — this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying questions before you model costs: 

1) For Dedicated capacity, how do burst windows work? If we commit to a monthly GPU pool but have short spikes during end-of-month processing, will that be covered or billed separately?
2) For Private VPC / on-prem, can you share typical lead time and what components stay in our network vs Redwood-managed control plane?
3) Can you model a base case (50M tokens/month) and a growth case (150M tokens/month) so procurement can compare economics?

Patricia from procurement is on copy — her timeline is tight (decision target by 2026-04-15). Also, we’ll need the SOC2 doc and the security questionnaire populated for legal.

Thanks,
Sam

Date: 2026-03-22T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & pricing — follow-up from today

Sam —

Thanks — looping in Aditya (SE) to build the cost models you asked for. High-level answers now: 
- Dedicated bursts: reserved capacity includes a configurable short burst window; beyond that we offer paid burst credits or transient hosted routing. We’ll call out burst SLAs in the quote.
- Private VPC lead time: typically 6–8 weeks for initial deployment (VPC peering, KMS integration, audit logs). On-prem increases that to ~10–14 weeks. Control plane can remain Redwood-hosted or customer-hosted depending on agreement.

Attaching our initial Dedicated pricing spreadsheet and SOC2 overview. Aditya — can you prepare a short per-token vs capacity model for 50M and 150M token scenarios and flag any assumptions we should validate with Sam’s team (e.g., embedding usage, long context models, KV cache hit rates)?

Proposed next steps:
- SE cost modeling call (30 min) this week — are you available Thurs/Fri?
- Procurement: Patricia, if you can share the security questionnaire, we’ll aim to fill the answers inline.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx, soc2-overview.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Lee <samuel.lee@finware.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-23T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & pricing — follow-up from today

Hi Sam / Team —

I put together an initial cost model (attached) and a short notes doc with assumptions. Highlights: 

- Hosted API (per-token): simplest to start. Using our standard gpt-ish generation price, 50M tokens/month estimates to ~$6k–$8k/month depending on model family and streaming efficiency. Pros: no infra ops; cons: higher unit cost at steady state and data in Redwood multi-tenant environment (we have contractual controls).

- Dedicated (reserved capacity): assuming a moderate-profile LLM and steady throughput, reserved commits can reduce unit cost by ~30–60% vs hosted per-token at scale. For 50M tokens, breakeven vs hosted is often at ~30–40M tokens/month depending on sequence length and batching. Dedicated offers predictable monthly invoices and isolation. See tab "50M_vs_150M" in the spreadsheet for numbers.

- Private VPC / on-prem: one-time onboarding + monthly platform fee. Lower ongoing infra op if you run it on your hardware, but higher TCO initially. Good fit if procurement requires full-network isolation or data residency.

Assumptions to validate: average tokens per request (you mentioned interactive flows ~150 tokens/request), peak concurrency, and whether you plan to cache prefixes or use embeddings heavily. If you can share sample request distribution, I’ll tighten the numbers.

I’m available for a 30-min modeling call Friday 2026-03-26 between 10:00–14:00 PT. If that works, I’ll walk through the spreadsheet line-by-line and produce a short one-page recommendation.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0214

Attachments: initial-cost-model.xlsx

- Patricia has attached the security questionnaire and our procurement checklist. Would appreciate SOC2 answers in the questionnaire and a short note on whether Dedicated meets our data isolation requirements.

I can do the modeling call Friday 2026-03-26 at 11:00 PT. Please send a calendar invite and a dial-in/meeting link.

Sam
